claim.pdf_says: D.3.2   Table definition   (a clause subordinate to "D.3   Tables and dynamic-length elementary items", printed in the same style and at the same numbering depth as "D.3.1   General")
claim.why_it_matters: D.3.1 is transcribed as "### D.3.1 General" (page 1057) but its sibling D.3.2 is transcribed at "##", the same level as its own parent "## D.3 Tables and dynamic-length elementary items". The markdown outline therefore shows D.3.2 as a peer of D.3 rather than a child of it, and D.3.1 as the only child. Any navigation, TOC generation or section-scoped citation built off the heading tree gets the wrong containment for the whole D.3 clause.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on four independent grounds. (1) Nothing is missing. The rendered PDF page 1058 (E:/Temp/specrecon/v1058/spec_p1058.png) prints the heading 'D.3.2 Table definition' and specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 42389 carries it verbatim as '## D.3.2 Table definition', preceded by its anchor '' at line 42388. The claim's own two quotations are the same text; it is filed as kind=missing-heading but identifies no missing text, only a markdown '#'-depth difference. (2) There is no level information in the PDF to lose. I rendered page 1057 and compared the printed glyphs directly: 'D.3 Tables and dynamic-length elementary items' and 'D.3.1 General' are set in the SAME bold face at the SAME point size, and 'D.3.2 Table definition' on page 1058 is set identically to both. ISO's Annex D gives depth-2 and depth-3 clause headings one uniform typographic style; containment is conveyed solely by the dotted clause number. The claim's premise that the print distinguishes a parent level from a child level is false — by its own visual test D.3 and D.3.1 are indistinguishable. The number 'D.3.2' is transcribed exactly, so every bit of hierarchy the PDF actually encodes survives intact. (3) The difference is page-break formatting furniture, which is an explicit rejection criterion. The reset to '##' happens precisely because D.3.2 is the first heading after the '## Page 1058' break; the transcription pipeline restarts nesting at each page boundary. This is not local to page 1058: the same reset occurs 166 times across the file (grep '^## D\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]' -> 166 hits), e.g. D.2.2.1 is '####' but D.2.2.2 is '##'; D.2.3.2.2 is '####' but D.2.3.2.3 is '##'; D.3.5.2 is '###' but D.3.5.3 is '##'. A document-wide pipeline artifact is not a page-1058 content discrepancy. (4) The stated consequence does not obtain. The transcription's own Annex D table of contents (lines 1054-1062) mirrors ISO's printed contents, lists only the depth-2 clauses D.1..D.9, and links by anchor ('[D.3 Tables and dynamic-length elementary items](#section-d-3)'). Navigation and section-scoped citation in this repository key off the clause number and the 'section-d-3-2' anchor, both of which are correct and unambiguous; neither reads markdown '#' depth. No word, number, rule or meaning differs between the PDF and the transcription on this page.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a discrepancy. The heading 'D.3.2 Table definition' is present verbatim in the markdown with a correct 'section-d-3-2' anchor; the PDF prints D.3, D.3.1 and D.3.2 in one identical bold style with hierarchy carried only by the clause number, which is transcribed exactly. The sole difference is the markdown '#' nesting depth ('##' rather than '###'), a page-boundary artifact of the page-by-page transcription that recurs 166 times document-wide and loses no content or meaning. If it is ever worth addressing, it is a single global re-nesting pass over the whole file driven by the dotted clause numbers, not a per-page structural finding.
